quotes.text: Bottom line, RAG is what turns a parrot into a real assistant. Done right, you get answers drawn from your tenant, filtered through your permissions, and grounded in sources that exist.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains in one line why grounding and permissions make RAG trustworthy.

quotes.text: Don't treat studio connectors as plug and play for critical systems, roadmap time and resources for extending them, or pivot the workload to foundry, where custom APIs and pipelines are first class citizens.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Practical warning about connector readiness in enterprise rollouts.

quotes.text: Don't obsess about which tool you should pick on day one, focus instead on which tier you're in.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes the platform debate as a lifecycle decision.

quotes.text: Studio buys you speed, Foundry buys you control. The pain just comes from different angles depending on which you ignore.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Concise trade-off summary between the two platforms.

quotes.text: And the real play is stacking them. Explore in studio, scale into Foundry and govern there when the auditors show up.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Memorable recommendation for a hybrid platform strategy.

takeaways: Retrieval-augmented generation with identity-aware access control is what turns a hallucinating chatbot into an assistant grounded in your tenant data.
Copilot Studio delivers fast low-code pilots but hides model controls, while Azure AI Foundry exposes models, evaluation, MLOps and audit trails at the cost of time and skills.

Use an explore, scale, govern progression: prototype in Studio, move to Foundry when non-Microsoft 365 data, hallucination risk or compliance requirements appear, and budget early for tokens, licensing and connector work.
hook: Most enterprise bots sound smart but hallucinate when asked about your real policies and data. This episode is for architects and IT leaders choosing between Copilot Studio and Azure AI Foundry. You learn how RAG works, where each platform shines and a simple framework for when to migrate.
